title: Joining Duke and learning the plunger from Tricky Sam
summary: Hired to play Bubber Miley's plunger role, he had never used one and learned it by listening to Tricky Sam Nanton.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: How did you get on with Fletcher?
All right.
He's a nice guy, don't you think?
Yeah.
I mean, he's a man, an easy going guy.
Yeah.
He didn't fuss anybody, did he?
No. No, we did our job, did our work.
Yeah.
And so I left and went up there with Duke. And I said -- I used to laugh when Tricky would start to blowing, you know. It sounded funny to me.
(Laughter)
I knowed there ain't no sound like that.
(Laughter)
I guess nobody had played a trombone with a plunger like that before, had they?
No. So I used to laugh.
What did Tricky say when you'd laugh?
He didn't say nothing. Till he come to me. Sitting up there playing, and he come to me, and I

said, "Well, this man hired me to play like that." So I kept on listening to Tricky. One night I had the plunger, and I said, "Wah, wah." And I woke up everybody, and they said, "That's it. That's it. Keep on. That's it. That's it. Keep on."
No kidding. Really?
Yeah.
How funny.
And I started to play on the plunger.
Isn't that funny.
By listening to Tricky. I'd go home and rehearse on it.
Oh, you would?
Uh-huh.
Because that takes a different kind of blowing altogether, doesn't it?
Uh-huh. A different kind of blowing altogether. Now, I'd never had a plunger in my hand until I went in there.
Is that right. So you didn't have any mute in the horn with the plunger, did you? Did you just use the plunger?
I just used the plunger starting off. Then I had to buy a mute.
Did Tricky use a mute?
Yeah. Tricky used a mute. But then some thing -- the majority of the time, he'd have the mute half cocked with the plunger.
Yeah.
I learned everything from him.
You did?
Yeah.
